title: Birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
commentary: Born on Monday morning, 9 Rabi' al-Awwal, in the Banu Hashim quarter of Makkah, in the Year of the Elephant.
His mother sent word to his grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib, who carried him to the Ka'bah, prayed to Allah and thanked Him, and named him Muhammad, a name not then common among the Arabs.
notes: The book gives 20 or 22 April 571 CE (per Muhammad Sulaiman Al-Mansourpuri and Mahmud Pasha); 20 April is used here as it falls on a Monday.
hijri-date: Monday 9 Rabi' al-Awwal, Year of the Elephant

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Nursed by Thuwaybah
commentary: After his mother, the first woman to nurse him was Thuwaybah, the concubine of Abu Lahab, along with her own son Masruh.
She had earlier nursed Hamzah bin 'Abdul-Muttalib and later nursed Abu Salamah bin 'Abd Al-Asad Al-Makhzumi.
notes: Approximate dates; the book gives no duration.
hijri-date: Rabi' al-Awwal, Year of the Elephant

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Circumcision on the seventh day
commentary: His grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib had him circumcised on his seventh day, as was the custom of the Arabs.
hijri-date: 16 Rabi' al-Awwal, Year of the Elephant

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: With Haleemah As-Sa'diyah among Banu Sa'd
commentary: Haleemah bint Abi Dhuaib of Banu Sa'd bin Bakr took him to the desert, after the other nursing women had refused him because he was an orphan.
Her household was blessed with milk, healthy flocks and green pasture while he was with them.
After two years, when he was weaned, she brought him back to his mother but begged to keep him longer, and he stayed with her until he was four or five.
notes: Approximate dates.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Gabriel opens his chest
commentary: Gabriel came to him, split open his chest, took out his heart and removed a blood clot from it, saying, "That was the part of Satan in thee"; he then washed it with Zamzam water in a golden basin and put it back in place.
His playmates ran to his nurse crying that Muhammad had been killed; they found him safe, but his face had turned pale.
notes: Approximate date (age four or five). Reported by Muslim on the authority of Anas.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Returned to his mother Aminah
commentary: Worried after the opening of his chest, Haleemah returned him to his mother, with whom he stayed until he was six.
notes: Approximate dates.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: His mother Aminah dies at Al-Abwa'
commentary: To visit her late husband's grave, Aminah made the 500 km journey to Yathrib with her orphaned son, her servant Umm Ayman and her father-in-law 'Abdul-Muttalib, and stayed there a month.
On the way back to Makkah she fell severely ill and died at Al-Abwa', on the road between Makkah and Madinah.
notes: Approximate date (age six).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: In the care of his grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib
commentary: 'Abdul-Muttalib brought the orphaned boy back to Makkah and favoured him even over his own children.
He let him sit on his own mattress in the shade of the Ka'bah, and when his uncles moved him away he would say: "Leave my grandson. By Allah, this boy will hold a significant position."
notes: Approximate dates.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of 'Abdul-Muttalib; Abu Talib takes charge
commentary: His grandfather 'Abdul-Muttalib died in Makkah when he was eight years, two months and ten days old.
His uncle Abu Talib, his father's brother, took charge of him, preferred him to his own children, and supported and protected him for forty years.
notes: Date calculated from the age the book gives.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Journey to Syria and the monk Bahira
commentary: At twelve he went with his uncle Abu Talib on a trading journey to Syria.

At Busra the monk Bahira recognised him by the seal of Prophethood below his shoulder and urged Abu Talib to take him back to Makkah for fear of the Jews; Abu Talib sent him back with some of his servants.
notes: Approximate date (age twelve).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Sacrilegious (Fijar) Wars
commentary: War broke out between Quraish and Banu Kinanah on one side and Qais 'Ailan on the other; it was called sacrilegious because it was fought even in the sacred months.
He attended one of its battles with his uncles but did not take up arms; he only picked up the enemy's arrows and handed them to his uncles.
notes: He was about fifteen; the wars lasted several years.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Fudul Confederacy (Hilf al-Fudul)
commentary: After the Fijar wars, Banu Hashim, Banu Al-Muttalib, Asad, Zahrah and Taim met in the house of 'Abdullah bin Jada'an and pledged to suppress injustice and uphold the rights of the weak.
It was prompted by a Zubaidi merchant whom Al-'As bin Wa'il refused to pay. He witnessed the pact and later said he would respond to such a call even in Islam.
notes: Approximate date; the book only says it followed the Fijar wars.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Trading in Syria for Khadijah
commentary: He had no fixed job in his youth, but is reported to have worked as a shepherd among Banu Sa'd and in Makkah. At twenty-five he took Khadijah's merchandise to Syria, accompanied by her servant Maisarah.
Hearing of his truthfulness, honesty and good manners, she sent for him and offered him a higher rate than she gave others.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Khadijah
commentary: On his return, Khadijah found more profit and blessing than usual, and Maisarah told her of his good manners and honesty, so she sent her friend Nafisa bint Maniya to propose to him.
He agreed, and his uncles arranged the marriage with her uncle. She was forty; the dowry was twenty camels, and he married no other woman while she lived.
She bore all his children except Ibrahim: Al-Qasim, Zainab, Ruqaiyah, Umm Kulthum, Fatimah and 'Abdullah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Rebuilding of the Ka'bah and the Black Stone
commentary: Five years before Prophethood a great flood almost demolished the Ka'bah. Quraish rebuilt it using only lawful money, leaving out Al-Hijr when that money ran short.
The clans quarrelled for four or five days over who would place the Black Stone, until Abu Umayyah bin Al-Mugheerah proposed that the first man to enter the Sanctuary should decide.
He was the first to enter, and they cried, "Al-Ameen has come." He placed the stone on a mantle, had the clans' representatives lift it together, then set it in place with his own hands.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Rebuilding Al-Ka‘bah and the Arbitration Issue

title: Retreats in the Cave of Hira'
commentary: As he neared forty he spent long periods in the Cave of Hira' on Mount An-Nour, two miles from Makkah, especially in Ramadan, taking barley porridge (sawiq) and water with him.
This period of seclusion lasted three years before the Revelation.
notes: Approximate start date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: In the Shade of the Message and Prophethood

title: First Revelation in the Cave of Hira'
commentary: Gabriel came to him in the Cave of Hira' with the first verses of Surah Al-'Alaq ("Read!").
He returned home shaken to Khadijah, who comforted him and took him to her cousin Waraqah bin Nawfal.
notes: This chapter is listed in the book's contents but missing from the supplied text file; the date (Monday night, 21 Ramadan, 10 August 610 CE, at forty lunar years and six months) is from the printed edition.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Three years of secret call
commentary: Because Makkah was the centre of idol worship guarded by Quraish, the call was kept secret at first so as not to provoke them.

Khadijah, Zaid bin Harithah, 'Ali bin Abi Talib and Abu Bakr embraced Islam on the very first day. Through Abu Bakr came 'Uthman bin 'Affan, Az-Zubair bin Al-'Awwam, 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf, Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas and Talhah bin 'Ubaidullah.
Prayer at that stage was two rak'ahs in the morning and two in the evening (Ghafir 40:55).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Pause in Revelation
commentary: Ibn Sa'd reported from Ibn 'Abbas that the Revelation paused for a few days; the book considers this most likely and rejects the claim that the pause lasted three and a half years.
He was deeply grieved, and Gabriel would appear to him and say: "O Muhammad! You are indeed Allah's Messenger in truth."
notes: Approximate dates ("a few days").

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Revelation resumes: "Arise and warn"
commentary: While walking he heard a voice and saw the angel of Hira' seated on a chair between earth and sky; he went home saying "Cover me", and Allah revealed the opening verses of Surah Al-Muddaththir (74:1-5).
After that, revelation came strongly, frequently and regularly.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Once more, Gabriel brings Allah’s Revelation

title: Open preaching begins
commentary: Allah commanded him to warn his nearest kinsmen (Ash-Shu'ara' 26:214). He gathered forty-five men of Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib; Abu Lahab spoke against him, while Abu Talib swore to protect him.
He then stood on Mount As-Safa and called the clans of Quraish to the Oneness of Allah; when Abu Lahab cursed him, "Perish the two hands of Abu Lahab" (Al-Masad 111:1) was revealed.
notes: Start of the fourth year of Prophethood.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: First blood shed in Islam
commentary: In the fourth year of Prophethood, polytheists spotted a group of Muslims on their way to a secret meeting with the Prophet in the hills of Makkah and attacked them; Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas struck one of them and drew his blood, the first blood shed in Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Organised persecution begins
commentary: After some months of ridicule, Quraish formed a committee of twenty-five notables chaired by Abu Lahab to organise a full-scale campaign against Islam.

Weaker converts were tortured: Bilal was laid on burning sand under heavy stones, and 'Ammar bin Yasir and his parents were tormented; his mother Sumaiyah was killed by Abu Jahl, becoming the first woman martyr in Islam.
notes: Late in the fourth year of Prophethood.
hijri-date: Late 10 BH (end of year 4 of Prophethood)

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Quraish agree to call him a sorcerer
commentary: A few months after the open call began, with the pilgrimage season approaching, Quraish gathered with Al-Waleed bin Al-Mugheerah to agree on one thing to say about him to the Arab pilgrims.

After rejecting soothsayer, madman and poet, they settled on calling him a sorcerer who separates a son from his father, a man from his brother, a wife from her husband and a man from his clan. Allah revealed verses about Al-Waleed (Al-Muddaththir 74:18-25).
notes: Shortly before the pilgrimage season; approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: An Advisory Council to debar Pilgrims from Muhammad’s Call

title: Dar Al-Arqam becomes the meeting place
commentary: In the fifth year of his mission he took the house of Al-Arqam on As-Safa as a temporary centre to meet his followers secretly and teach them the Qur'an and Islamic wisdom.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: First migration to Abyssinia
commentary: As persecution became unbearable, Surah Al-Kahf and Surah Az-Zumar (39:10) pointed to emigration, and he permitted some followers to seek refuge with the just Negus of Abyssinia.
In Rajab of the fifth year of Prophethood, twelve men and four women, including 'Uthman bin 'Affan and his wife Ruqaiyah, the Prophet's daughter, slipped out of Makkah by night.
They sailed from the port of Shu'aibah; Quraish sent men after them, but they had already left, and they were warmly received in Abyssinia.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Recitation of Surah An-Najm at the Ka'bah
commentary: In Ramadan of the same year he recited Surah An-Najm before a large gathering of Quraish at the Sanctuary; when he reached its final verse (An-Najm 53:62) and prostrated, the polytheists all prostrated with him.
Blamed by those who had not been present, they then spread the lie that he had praised their idols, to excuse their prostration.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Emigrants return from Abyssinia
commentary: A false report reached the emigrants that all of Quraish had embraced Islam, so they set out for home and reached Makkah in Shawwal of the same year.
An hour's journey from Makkah they learned the truth: some went back to Abyssinia, while others entered the city secretly or openly under the protection of a notable.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Second migration to Abyssinia
commentary: As torture grew worse, a larger group left: eighty-three men and eighteen or nineteen women.
notes: Approximate date; the book only says it followed the return of the first group.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Quraish envoys at the court of the Negus
commentary: Quraish sent 'Amr bin Al-'As and 'Abdullah bin Abi Rabi'a with gifts to have the Muslims handed back.

Ja'far bin Abi Talib explained Islam and recited the opening of Surah Maryam, and the next day stated their belief about Jesus. The Negus refused to give them up, returned the gifts and guaranteed their safety.
notes: Approximate date; the book does not date this embassy.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Quraish pressure Abu Talib
commentary: Quraish again pressed Abu Talib to stop his nephew. The Prophet said he would not give up his mission even if they put the sun in his right hand and the moon in his left, and Abu Talib promised never to forsake him.
Later they offered him the youth 'Amarah bin Al-Waleed as a son in exchange for his nephew, so that they could kill him. Abu Talib refused.
notes: The book places these meetings in the sixth year, a short time apart.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Once more Quraish approaches Abu Talib

title: Hamzah bin 'Abdul-Muttalib accepts Islam
commentary: Returning from a hunt, Hamzah learned that Abu Jahl had abused his nephew at As-Safa and wounded his head. He struck Abu Jahl on the head with his bow and declared his Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab accepts Islam
commentary: Three days after Hamzah, 'Umar, until then a bitter opponent, read the opening of Surah Ta-Ha at his sister Fatimah's house and went to the Prophet to accept Islam.
After his conversion the Muslims began to worship openly at the Ka'bah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: 'Utbah bin Rabi'a's offer
commentary: Quraish sent 'Utbah bin Rabi'a to offer him wealth, leadership, kingship or a cure if he gave up his call. He answered by reciting the opening of Surah Fussilat, and 'Utbah went back with a changed face, advising Quraish to leave him alone.
notes: Approximate date; the book says it was shortly after Hamzah and 'Umar accepted Islam. In another version 'Utbah stopped him at Fussilat 41:13.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Quraish’s Representative negotiates with the Messenger of Allah [pbuh]

title: Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib pledge protection
commentary: Abu Talib gathered Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib, Muslims and non-Muslims, to protect the Prophet. Only Abu Lahab refused and sided with Quraish.
notes: The book says Hamzah's and 'Umar's conversions, his refusal of any compromise and this pact all happened within less than four weeks.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Abu Talib assembles Bani Hashim and Bani Al-Muttalib

title: The boycott in Shi'b Abi Talib
commentary: Meeting at Wadi Al-Muhassab, Quraish wrote a pact, hung inside the Ka'bah, to boycott Banu Hashim and Banu Al-Muttalib in marriage, trade and contact until the Prophet was handed over to be killed.
From Muharram of the seventh year they were confined in Shi'b Abi Talib for three years, eating leaves and skins, while a few sympathetic Makkans smuggled in food.
hijri-date: Muharram 7 BH - Muharram 4 BH (from year 7 of Prophethood)

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: A Pact of Injustice and Aggression

title: The boycott ends
commentary: Five Makkans, led by Hisham bin 'Amr and Zuhair bin Abi Omaiyah, campaigned at the Ka'bah to annul the pact.
Abu Talib told them it had been revealed to his nephew that ants had eaten the parchment except for the Name of Allah. Al-Mut'im bin 'Adi found it so, and the pact was annulled.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: A Pact of Injustice and Aggression

title: Death of Abu Talib
commentary: Six months after leaving the valley, Abu Talib fell ill and died. On his deathbed the Prophet urged him to declare that there is no god but Allah, but he died on the religion of 'Abdul-Muttalib.
The verses At-Tawbah 9:113 and Al-Qasas 28:56 were then revealed.
notes: Another report says Ramadan, three days before Khadijah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of Khadijah
commentary: Two months after Abu Talib, Khadijah died at sixty-five, when he was fifty. She had shared his trials for twenty-five years.
The Prophet called that year the Year of Grief.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Khadijah passes away to the Mercy of Allâh

title: Marriage to Sawdah bint Zam'a
commentary: An early Muslim who had persuaded her husband As-Sakran bin 'Amr to accept Islam, Sawdah went with him on the second migration to Abyssinia and was widowed when he died on the way back. She was the first woman he married after Khadijah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: His Marriage to Sawdah [R] in Shawwal, the tenth year of Prophethood

title: Journey to At-Ta'if
commentary: With his freed slave Zaid bin Harithah he went to At-Ta'if, about 60 km from Makkah, to call Thaqif to Islam; its chiefs mocked him.

After ten days the townspeople stoned him out of the city until his legs bled. Resting in an orchard he made his well-known supplication, and 'Addas, a Christian servant of Rabi'a's two sons, kissed his hands.
On the way back, at Qarn Al-Manazil, he declined the angel of the mountains' offer to crush Makkah, hoping that their descendants would worship Allah.
notes: The book dates it to late May or early June 619 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Third Phase: Calling unto Islam beyond Makkah

title: The jinn listen to the Qur'an at Nakhlah
commentary: On the way back from At-Ta'if he stayed a few days at Wadi Nakhlah, where a group of jinn listened to his recitation and believed, as described in Al-Ahqaf 46:29-31 and Al-Jinn 72:1-2. He did not know of them until these verses were revealed.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Third Phase: Calling unto Islam beyond Makkah

title: Calling the tribes at the pilgrimage season
commentary: He returned to presenting Islam to the visiting tribes and individuals as the pilgrimage season approached, as he had done since the fourth year.
Among the tribes he approached were Banu 'Amir bin Sa'sa'ah, Kindah, Kalb and Banu Haneefah, but none of them responded.
notes: The book dates this to July 619 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Islam being introduced to Arabian Tribes and Individuals

title: Swaid, Eyas, Abu Dhar, Tufail and Dhumad accept Islam
commentary: Individuals from outside Makkah accepted Islam: Swaid bin Samit and the youth Eyas bin Mu'adh of Yathrib, Abu Dhar Al-Ghifari, Tufail bin 'Amr Ad-Dausi, chief of Daus, and Dhumad Al-Azdi from Yemen.
notes: The book lists them after the pilgrimage season of the tenth year, and dates Swaid's account and Tufail's arrival in Makkah to the eleventh year.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Islam being introduced to Arabian Tribes and Individuals

title: Marriage contract with 'Aishah
commentary: He concluded a marriage contract with 'Aishah, daughter of Abu Bakr, when she was six. The marriage was consummated in Madinah in Shawwal of 1 AH, when she was nine.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Six men from Yathrib accept Islam at 'Aqabah
commentary: At 'Aqabah in Mina he met six men from Yathrib, including As'ad bin Zurarah. Having heard the Jews speak of a coming Prophet, they accepted Islam and took the message home.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Hope inspiring Breezes from the Madinese

title: First Pledge of 'Aqabah
commentary: Twelve men from Yathrib, five of them from the previous year's six, pledged at 'Aqabah to worship Allah alone, not to steal, commit adultery, kill their children or slander, and not to disobey him in any just matter.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Mus'ab bin 'Umair sent to Yathrib
commentary: Mus'ab bin 'Umair went to Yathrib as the first Muslim envoy, staying with As'ad bin Zurarah. Sa'd bin Mu'adh and Usaid bin Hudair accepted Islam, and in time every house of the Ansar except one family had Muslims in it.
He returned to Makkah before the next pilgrimage with good news.
hijri-date: Dhul-Hijjah 2 BH - Dhul-Qa'dah 1 BH (from year 12 of Prophethood)

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Al-Isra' and Al-Mi'raj (Night Journey and Ascension)
commentary: He was carried on Al-Buraq with Gabriel from the Sacred Mosque in Makkah to Al-Aqsa in Jerusalem, where he led the Prophets in prayer.
He then ascended through the heavens, met earlier Prophets, and was given fifty daily prayers, reduced at his request to five.
notes: The exact date is disputed; most jurists place it 12 to 16 months before the Hijrah. The author suggests it was before the First Pledge of 'Aqabah or between the two pledges.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Second Pledge of 'Aqabah
commentary: Seventy-three men and two women from Yathrib met him secretly at night at 'Aqabah during the days of Tashreeq; his uncle Al-'Abbas came with him.
They pledged to listen and obey, to spend in plenty and in scarcity, and to protect him as they protected their own families. Twelve deputies were chosen, nine from Al-Khazraj and three from Al-Aws.
notes: The book gives June 622 CE and "mid Tashreeq days" (11-13 Dhul-Hijjah); the day is calculated. The narrative says "over seventy"; Ka'b bin Malik's account gives seventy-three men and two women.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Muslims begin emigrating to Madinah
commentary: After the pledge he allowed the Muslims to emigrate. Quraish tried to stop them, and many had to leave their wealth behind.
Suhaib gave up all his wealth to leave, Hisham bin Al-'Asi was detained, and 'Ayyash bin Abi Rabi'a, who had left with 'Umar, was tricked back to Makkah and tied up.
Within two months almost all the Muslims had left, except the Prophet, Abu Bakr, 'Ali and those held back.
notes: Approximate dates. The book notes that Abu Salamah, the first to emigrate, left a year before the Second Pledge, and his wife Umm Salamah was kept from him for a year.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Quraish plot to kill him at Dar An-Nadwah
commentary: Quraish's leaders met in their council house, rejected expelling or imprisoning him, and adopted Abu Jahl's plan: a young man from every clan would strike him together, so the blood-money would be shared by all clans.
notes: The book prints 12 September 622 CE, which is in the proleptic Gregorian calendar; converted here to the Julian calendar used throughout this file.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Hijrah: he leaves his house
commentary: Told of the plot by Gabriel, he left 'Ali sleeping in his bed and walked out past the men waiting at his door, casting dust at them and reciting Ya-Sin 36:9.
With Abu Bakr he went south toward Yemen instead of north, to Mount Thawr.
notes: The book prints 12/13 September 622 CE, which is in the proleptic Gregorian calendar; converted here to the Julian calendar used throughout this file.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Three nights in the Cave of Thawr
commentary: They hid in the cave for three nights, Friday, Saturday and Sunday. 'Abdullah bin Abi Bakr brought them news each night, and 'Amir bin Fuhairah brought Abu Bakr's goats every evening to give them milk.
Quraish set a reward of 100 camels for each of them. The searchers reached the mouth of the cave, and the Prophet calmed Abu Bakr: "What do you think of those two with whom the Third is Allah?"

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Journey along the coastal route
commentary: Guided by 'Abdullah bin Uraiquit, they took little-used coastal roads. Suraqah bin Malik chased them for the reward, but his horse kept stumbling until he asked for pardon; at Umm Ma'bad's tents her dry goat gave milk.
Asma' bint Abi Bakr tore her waistband in two to tie the provisions, earning the name "she of the two waistbands".

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Arrival at Quba' and the Quba' Mosque
commentary: He reached Quba' and stayed four days with Kulthum bin Al-Hadm of Banu 'Amr bin 'Awf, laying the foundation of the Quba' Mosque.
'Ali stayed in Makkah three days to return what people had left with the Prophet for safekeeping, then joined him.
notes: The book prints 23 September 622 CE, which is in the proleptic Gregorian calendar; converted here to the Julian calendar used throughout this file.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Entry into Madinah and the first Friday prayer
commentary: He prayed the first Friday prayer with a hundred others in the vale of Banu Salim, then rode on into the city amid crowds of welcomers.
He let his camel go, saying it was commanded by Allah; it knelt in the quarter of Banu An-Najjar, his maternal relatives, and he stayed with Abu Ayyub Al-Ansari.
notes: The book (p. 118) prints Friday 12 Rabi' al-Awwal 1 AH, i.e. 27 September 622 CE, which is in the proleptic Gregorian calendar; converted here to the Julian calendar used throughout this file.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Building the Prophet's Mosque
commentary: His first task was to build a mosque on the site where his camel had knelt, on land bought from two orphans. He carried adobe bricks and stones himself, and rooms for his household were built beside it.
The call to prayer (Adhan) was introduced at this early stage.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Brotherhood between Emigrants and Helpers
commentary: In the house of Anas bin Malik he paired ninety men, half Emigrants and half Helpers, as brothers with real duties of mutual support; such brothers even inherited from each other until Al-Anfal 8:75 was revealed at the time of Badr.
Sa'd bin Ar-Rabi' offered half his wealth to his brother 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf, who declined and asked only to be shown the market.
hijri-date: 1 AH, after the Mosque was built

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Charter of Islamic Alliance and the pact with the Jews
commentary: He drew up a charter making the Emigrants and Helpers one nation, and a pact of cooperation and non-aggression with the Jews of Madinah: each kept its own religion, each would help the other if attacked, and all would defend Madinah.
notes: The pact with the Jews is described under 'A Cooperation and Non-Aggression Pact with the Jews' (p. 124).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition of Saif Al-Bahr (Hamzah)
commentary: Hamzah bin 'Abdul-Muttalib led thirty Emigrants to intercept a Quraish caravan of 300 men including Abu Jahl. The two sides lined up to fight, but Majdi bin 'Amr, on good terms with both, prevented a clash.
On this occasion the Prophet gave the first flag in Muslim history; it was white and was carried by Kinaz bin Husain Al-Ghanawi.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: 'Aishah joins his household
commentary: His marriage to 'Aishah, contracted in Makkah when she was six, was consummated in Madinah in Shawwal 1 AH, seven months after the Hijrah, when she was nine.
notes: 'Seven months after the Hijrah' is from 'The Prophet Household' (p. 311).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition to Batn Rabigh ('Ubaidah)
commentary: 'Ubaidah bin Al-Harith led sixty Emigrant horsemen to Batn Rabigh and met Abu Sufyan at the head of a caravan of 200 men. Arrows were shot but there was no real fighting, and two Muslims in the caravan, Al-Miqdad bin 'Amr and 'Utbah bin Ghazwan, crossed over to 'Ubaidah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition to Al-Kharrar (Sa'd)
commentary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas led twenty horsemen to Al-Kharrar, but after a five-day march they found that the Quraish caravan had left the day before.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Al-Abwa' (Waddan)
commentary: His first expedition in person: he led seventy men, mostly Emigrants, to intercept a Quraish caravan but found none at Waddan. He made a non-aggression pact with Banu Damrah, and the expedition lasted fifteen days.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Buwat
commentary: He led 200 Companions toward a Quraish caravan of 100 men, including Umaiyah bin Khalaf, and 2,500 camels, but it had already left when he reached Buwat.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Safwan (first Badr)
commentary: Karz bin Jabir raided Madinah's pastures and drove off some animals. He chased him with seventy men as far as Safwan near Badr without catching him; it became known as the preliminary Badr expedition.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Dhul 'Ushairah
commentary: With 150-200 men and thirty camels ridden in turns, he set out to intercept a Quraish caravan, but it had left Dhul 'Ushairah some days before. It was this caravan, on its return from Syria, that led to Badr. He made a non-aggression pact with Banu Mudlij and their allies Banu Damrah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition to Nakhlah ('Abdullah bin Jahsh)
commentary: 'Abdullah bin Jahsh led twelve Emigrants to Nakhlah to gather news of Quraish. They attacked a caravan in Rajab, a sacred month, killing 'Amr bin Al-Hadrami and capturing two men.

The Prophet disapproved, and Quraish accused the Muslims of violating the sacred month; Al-Baqarah 2:217 was revealed in answer. The two captives were later released and blood money was paid for the dead man.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Fighting is made obligatory
commentary: In Sha'ban 2 AH the Muslims were ordered to fight those who fought them, without transgressing the limits (Al-Baqarah 2:190-193).
notes: The book says the earlier permission to fight (Al-Hajj 22:39) was revealed in Madinah after the Hijrah, but its exact date is uncertain.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Qiblah changed to the Ka'bah
commentary: The direction of prayer was changed from Jerusalem to the Sacred Mosque in Makkah. This exposed the hypocrites among the Jews and others weak at heart.
notes: The book gives February 624 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of Ruqaiyah, his daughter
commentary: News of the victory at Badr reached Madinah just after his daughter Ruqaiyah, wife of 'Uthman bin 'Affan, was buried. She had been gravely ill, and the Prophet had asked 'Uthman to stay in Madinah to look after her.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Madinah receives the News of Victory

title: Fasting of Ramadan and Zakat made obligatory
commentary: Fasting in Ramadan was made obligatory in 2 AH, together with the duty of paying Zakat, to ease the burden of the needy Emigrants.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Battle of Badr in its Qur’ânic Context

title: The Battle of Badr
commentary: Setting out after Abu Sufyan's caravan, 300-317 Muslims with two horses and seventy camels met a Makkan army of about 1,000 at Badr after the caravan had escaped.
The Muslims won decisively: fourteen were martyred, while seventy polytheists, including Abu Jahl, were killed and seventy captured.
notes: The book says: 'That was Friday night, Ramadan 17th, the year 2 A.H.' The calculated date was moved to the Friday.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The first 'Eid al-Fitr
commentary: The first 'Eid of breaking the fast was established directly after the victory at Badr, with the Muslims going out praying and praising Allah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Battle of Badr in its Qur’ânic Context

title: Ghazwah of Al-Kudr
commentary: Hearing that Banu Saleem of Ghatfan were mustering troops, he made a surprise raid on them at the watering place of Al-Kudr, seven days after Badr. They had fled; he stayed three days and took their 500 camels as booty.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Plot by 'Umair bin Wahb to kill him
commentary: Safwan bin Umaiyah promised to pay 'Umair bin Wahb's debts and support his family, so 'Umair came to Madinah with a poisoned sword to kill the Prophet. The Prophet revealed to him his secret plan with Safwan, and 'Umair accepted Islam.
notes: The book gives no date; it places the attempt after Badr.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: An Attempt on the Life of the Prophet [pbuh]

title: Siege of Banu Qainuqa'
commentary: Banu Qainuqa', the first Jews to break the pact, harassed Muslims in their market. When a Jewish goldsmith exposed a Muslim woman, a Muslim killed him and the Jews killed that Muslim, and fighting began.
He besieged their forts for fifteen days until they surrendered to his judgement. He accepted the intercession of 'Abdullah bin Ubai, and they were expelled to Azru'a in Syria.
notes: The book prints Saturday 15 Shawwal 2 AH; the calculated date was moved to the nearest Saturday.
hijri-date: Saturday 15 Shawwal 2 AH, siege of 15 days

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Qainuqa‘ Jews breach the Covenant

title: Ghazwah of As-Sawiq
commentary: Vowing revenge for Badr, Abu Sufyan set out with 200 men; his raiders burnt palm trees at Al-'Uraid near Madinah and killed two Muslims. When pursued, they threw away their provisions of sawiq (barley porridge) to flee faster.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage of Fatimah and 'Ali
commentary: His daughter Fatimah was married to 'Ali bin Abi Talib in the period between the battles of Badr and Uhud.
notes: The book gives no exact date, only the period between Badr and Uhud.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Dhi Amr
commentary: Hearing that Banu Tha'labah and Banu Muharib were mustering to raid the outskirts of Madinah, he led 450 men against them. They scattered into the mountains, and the Muslims camped at Dhi Amr for all of Safar.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Hafsah bint 'Umar
commentary: Hafsah, daughter of 'Umar, had lost her husband Khunais bin Hudhafa As-Sahmi between Badr and Uhud; the Prophet married her in the third year of the Hijrah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Killing of Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf
commentary: Ka'b bin Al-Ashraf, a Jewish poet who satirised the Prophet, incited Quraish after Badr and defamed Muslim women in his verses, was killed at night by Muhammad bin Maslamah, Abu Na'ilah and their companions.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Buhran
commentary: In Rabi' al-Thani 3 AH he led 300 men to Buhran in the area of Al-Furu' and stayed there until Jumada al-Ula. There was no fighting.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Zaid bin Harithah seizes a Quraish caravan
commentary: Quraish sent a caravan led by Safwan bin Omaiyah along a new route across Najd to Iraq. Zaid bin Harithah with 100 horsemen surprised it at Al-Qardah and seized goods worth 100,000 dirhams; it was the most successful campaign before Uhud.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Zaid bin Harithah leads a Campaign on the Trade Routes of Quraish

title: The Battle of Uhud
commentary: Quraish marched with 3,000 men. Of 1,000 Muslims, 'Abdullah bin Ubai withdrew with 300.
Early success turned into a reverse when forty of the fifty archers left their post. Khalid bin Al-Waleed's cavalry then attacked from behind, and the Prophet was wounded.
Seventy Muslims were martyred, among them Hamzah. Twenty-two (some say thirty-seven) polytheists were killed.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Hamra' Al-Asad
commentary: The day after Uhud, the Prophet set out in pursuit of Quraish with only those who had fought at Uhud, and camped at Hamra' Al-Asad, about eight miles from Madinah, for three days (Monday to Wednesday). News of the march, carried by Ma'bad bin Abi Ma'bad, made Abu Sufyan's army give up returning to attack Madinah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition of Abu Salamah to Banu Asad
commentary: Abu Salamah led 150 Emigrants and Helpers and took Banu Asad bin Khuzaimah by surprise in their own land as they gathered to fight, dispersing them. On his return his Uhud wound flared up, and he died soon afterwards.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Zainab bint Khuzaimah
commentary: Zainab, of Bani Hilal bin 'Amir, was called Umm Al-Masakeen (Mother of the Poor) for her kindness to them. The widow of 'Abdullah bin Jahsh, who was martyred at Uhud, she married the Prophet in 4 AH and died two or three months later.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Errand of 'Abdullah bin Unais
commentary: On 5 Muharram 4 AH news came that Khalid bin Sufyan Al-Hudhali was gathering men to raid the Muslims, and 'Abdullah bin Unais was sent against him. After eighteen days he returned to Madinah with Khalid's head, and the Prophet gave him a stick as a sign between them on the Day of Resurrection.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: An Errand led by ‘Abdullah bin Unais

title: The tragedy of Ar-Raji'
commentary: Companions sent to teach the tribes of 'Udal and Qarah (six, or ten in another version) were attacked at Ar-Raji' by a hundred archers of Banu Lihyan. Most were killed, and Khubaib and Zaid bin Ad-Dathna were taken, sold in Makkah and executed.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The tragedy of Bi'r Ma'unah
commentary: Seventy Companions learned in the Qur'an (forty according to Ibn Ishaq), sent to call the people of Najd to Islam under Abu Bara's protection, were massacred at Ma'unah Well by the Banu Saleem clans of 'Usaiyah, Ri'l and Dhakwan, whom 'Amir bin At-Tufail had called out. For thirty days the Prophet invoked Allah against the killers in the dawn prayer.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expulsion of Banu An-Nadeer
commentary: Banu An-Nadeer plotted to drop a millstone on the Prophet while he sat by a wall of their houses. After a siege of six nights (fifteen in another version) they agreed to leave with what their camels could carry, except arms, and went out with 600 loaded camels; their chiefs settled in Khaibar and another party went to Syria.
Almost all the verses of Surah Al-Hashr concern their banishment.
notes: The book gives August 625 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The second Badr (Badr Al-Maw'id)
commentary: Keeping the appointment Abu Sufyan had made at Uhud, the Prophet went to Badr with 1,500 men and ten horsemen. Abu Sufyan set out with 2,000 men but turned back from Mar Az-Zahran, while the Muslims waited eight days at Badr and sold their goods at double the price.
notes: The book gives January 626 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Invasion of Badr, the Second

title: Marriage to Umm Salamah
commentary: Umm Salamah Hind bint Abi Omaiyah, of Banu Makhzum, was the widow of Abu Salamah, who died in Jumada al-Akhirah 4 AH. The Prophet married her in Shawwal of the same year.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Dumat Al-Jandal
commentary: Told that tribes around Dumat Al-Jandal, on the Syrian border, were robbing travellers and gathering to raid Madinah, the Prophet led 1,000 men there, marching by night. The tribes fled; he stayed five days and, on the way back, made a peace treaty with 'Uyainah bin Hisn.
notes: The book says late Rabi' al-Awwal; the day shown is approximate.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Battle of the Trench (Al-Ahzab)
commentary: Jewish leaders rallied Quraish, Ghatfan and other tribes into an army of 10,000. On Salman Al-Farisi's advice the Muslims dug a trench, and 3,000 Muslims held it.
The siege lasted over a month until discord among the allies and a cold, violent wind drove them away.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Siege of Banu Quraiza
commentary: Banu Quraiza had broken their pact with the Muslims during the Battle of the Trench. After a siege of twenty-five days they accepted the judgement of Sa'd bin Mu'adh, who ruled that their fighting men be killed and their women and children taken captive. Sa'd died soon afterwards of the wound he had received at the Trench.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Zainab bint Jahsh
commentary: The Prophet's paternal cousin Zainab, of Bani Asad bin Khuzaimah, had been divorced by Zaid bin Harithah. Allah gave her to the Prophet in marriage (Al-Ahzab 33:37), and he married her at the time of the siege of Banu Quraiza. The marriage was meant to uproot the pre-Islamic custom of treating an adopted son as a real son.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Killing of Abu Rafi' Salam bin Abi Al-Huqaiq
commentary: Abu Rafi' Salam bin Abi Al-Huqaiq, who had mustered and funded the Confederates, was killed in his fort at Khaibar by a party of five from Al-Khazraj under 'Abdullah bin 'Ateeq. 'Abdullah struck him down and broke his leg on the way out, and the Prophet wiped it and it healed; another version says all five took part in the killing.
notes: The book gives Dhul-Qa'dah or Dhul-Hijjah 5 AH; the date shown is the start of Dhul-Hijjah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition to Banu Bakr; Thumamah captured
commentary: Muhammad bin Maslamah's thirty men raided Banu Bakr and brought back Thumamah bin Uthal Al-Hanafi, chief of Banu Hanifah, who had set out to assassinate the Prophet. He was tied to a pillar of the Mosque until the Prophet ordered his release, after which he washed and accepted Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Banu Lihyan
commentary: To avenge the ten Companions Banu Lihyan had betrayed at Ar-Raji', the Prophet marched with 200 men, feigning a march towards Syria. Banu Lihyan fled to the mountain tops, and the expedition lasted fourteen days.
notes: The book gives Rabi' al-Awwal or Jumada al-Ula 6 AH; the date shown lies between the two.
hijri-date: Rabi' al-Awwal or Jumada al-Ula 6 AH

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Zaid at Al-'Ais; Abul-'As returns to Zainab
commentary: Zaid bin Harithah with 170 horsemen intercepted at Al-'Ais a Quraish caravan led by Abul-'As, husband of the Prophet's daughter Zainab. Abul-'As took refuge with Zainab; at the Prophet's recommendation the Muslims returned his wealth, and he later accepted Islam, emigrated, and was reunited with her.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Zaid's patrol to Wadi Al-Qura
commentary: Zaid led a twelve-man reconnaissance patrol to Wadi Al-Qura. The people there attacked them and killed nine; Zaid and the others escaped.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Banu Al-Mustaliq (Al-Muraisi')
commentary: News came on 2 Sha'ban that Al-Harith bin Dirar, chief of Banu Al-Mustaliq, was gathering men to attack Madinah. The two sides met at the well of Al-Muraisi'; after an hour of arrow-shooting the Muslims charged and won, losing only one man, killed by mistake.
During this campaign 'Abdullah bin Ubai stirred up a quarrel between the Emigrants and the Helpers and swore that the most honourable would expel the meanest from Madinah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Juwairiyah bint Al-Harith
commentary: Juwairiyah, daughter of Al-Harith, head of Banu Al-Mustaliq, was among the captives and fell to Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, who made a covenant to set her free. The Prophet fulfilled the covenant and married her, and on that occasion his Companions set free a hundred families of her people.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The slander against 'Aishah (Al-Ifk)
commentary: On the return from Al-Muraisi', 'Aishah went back to look for a lost necklace, was left behind, and was brought to Madinah by Safwan bin Mu'attal. The hypocrites, led by 'Abdullah bin Ubai, spread a slander against her.

After she had been ill for a month and then learned of the slander, verses of Surah An-Nur (24:11) declared her innocence. Mistah bin Athatha, Hassan bin Thabit and Hamnah bint Jahsh were flogged eighty stripes.
notes: Approximate dates.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf at Dumat Al-Jandal
commentary: 'Abdur-Rahman bin 'Awf was sent to Banu Kalb at Dumat Al-Jandal. He stayed three days inviting them to Islam; they accepted, and he married their king's daughter Tamadur bint Al-Asbagh.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Delegations and Expeditions following Al-Muraisi‘ Ghazwah

title: 'Ali's expedition to Banu Sa'd at Fadak
commentary: 'Ali led a platoon against Banu Sa'd bin Bakr at Fadak, who had gathered to support the Jews of Khaibar. Banu Sa'd fled, and he took 500 camels and 2,000 goats.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Delegations and Expeditions following Al-Muraisi‘ Ghazwah

title: Expedition against Fazarah at Wadi Al-Qura
commentary: After Fazarah attempted the Prophet's life, a force under Abu Bakr (or Zaid bin Harithah) attacked them after the dawn prayer, killing some and capturing others, including Umm Qirfa.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Delegations and Expeditions following Al-Muraisi‘ Ghazwah

title: Treaty of Al-Hudaibiyah and Bay'at Ar-Ridwan
commentary: Following a dream, the Prophet set out for 'Umrah with 1,500 Muslims, carrying no weapons but sheathed swords. Quraish blocked the way, and he camped at Al-Hudaibiyah.
When 'Uthman, sent as envoy to Quraish, was delayed and feared killed, the Companions pledged under the tree to lay down their lives (Bay'at Ar-Ridwan, Al-Fath 48:18).
A truce suspending war for ten years was agreed: the Muslims would return that year and come back for 'Umrah the next. Surah Al-Fath (48:1) called it a manifest victory.
notes: The book gives 1,500 men at the start of the account and 1,400 later.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Letters to kings and rulers
commentary: On his return from Al-Hudaibiyah the Prophet had a silver seal engraved "Muhammad the Messenger of Allah" and sent envoys calling rulers to Islam: the Negus of Abyssinia, Muqawqas of Egypt, Chosroes of Persia, Caesar (Hercules) of the Byzantines, Mundhir bin Sawa of Bahrain, Haudha bin 'Ali of Yamama, Harith bin Abi Shamir Al-Ghassani of Damascus, and Jaifer and 'Abd Al-Jalandi of 'Oman.
Chosroes tore up his letter. Muqawqas did not accept Islam but sent gifts, including Maria, who bore the Prophet's son Ibrahim.
notes: Decided late in 6 AH on the return from Al-Hudaibiyah; the envoys left in Muharram 7 AH, a few days before Khaibar. The book says the letter to 'Oman was most likely sent much later, after the conquest of Makkah, and that the text of the letter to the Negus may date from the Makkan period.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Prophet’s Plans to spread the Message of Islam beyond Arabia

title: Marriage to Umm Habibah
commentary: Umm Habibah (Ramlah), daughter of Abu Sufyan, stood firm in Islam in Abyssinia after her husband 'Ubaidullah bin Jahsh became a Christian and died there. The Prophet sent 'Amr bin Omaiyah Ad-Damri with a letter to the Negus asking for her hand; the Negus agreed and sent her to him with Sharhabeel bin Hasnah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ghazwah of Dhu Qarad (Al-Ghabah)
commentary: Raiders of Bani Fazarah under 'Abdur Rahman Al-Fazari drove off the Prophet's camels. Salamah bin Al-Akwa' pursued them alone on foot, shooting arrows, and recovered all the camels; the Prophet called him the best footman of the day.
notes: Three days before Khaibar, according to most scholars.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Conquest of Khaibar
commentary: He marched on Khaibar, the fortified Jewish centre 60-80 miles north of Madinah, with 1,400 men. He gave the banner to 'Ali, and the forts fell one after another.
The Jews were allowed to stay and farm the land, giving half of its produce to the Muslims.
notes: The book dates the campaign to Muharram 7 AH; the end date is estimated.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Khalid bin Al-Waleed and 'Amr bin Al-'As accept Islam
commentary: 'Amr bin Al-'As, Khalid bin Al-Waleed and 'Uthman bin Talhah came to the Prophet and accepted Islam. On their arrival he said: "Quraish has given us its own blood."
notes: The book places this early in 7 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Ja'far and the Abyssinia emigrants return
commentary: As Khaibar was conquered, Ja'far bin Abi Talib and his companions arrived from Abyssinia, with Abu Musa Al-Ash'ari and some other Muslims. The Negus had sent them back at the Prophet's request, sixteen men with their wives and children on two boats, and the Prophet gave them shares of the spoils.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Safiyah bint Huyai
commentary: Safiyah, daughter of Huyai bin Akhtab, was among the captives of Khaibar; her husband Kinanah bin Abi Al-Huqaiq had been killed for treachery. The Prophet invited her to Islam and, when she accepted, freed and married her; the wedding feast was held on the way back at Sadd As-Sahba'.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The poisoned sheep at Khaibar
commentary: After the conquest, Zainab bint Al-Harith, a Jewish woman, offered him a poisoned roast sheep. He took a mouthful and spat it out; she confessed, and when his Companion Bishr bin Al-Bara' died of the poison, he ordered her to be killed.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Fadak surrenders; Wadi Al-Qura and Taima'
commentary: The people of Fadak asked for peace and were given terms like those of Khaibar; Fadak belonged to the Prophet alone, as no fighting took place there. Wadi Al-Qura surrendered after about two days of fighting, and the Jews of Taima' made peace, agreeing to pay tribute.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: At-Tufail arrives with the Daws
commentary: At-Tufail bin 'Amr Ad-Dawsi, whose people had at last embraced Islam, came with seventy or eighty families of Daws and caught up with the Prophet at Khaibar.
notes: The book dates this to early 7 AH, while the Prophet was at Khaibar.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Return to Madinah from Khaibar
commentary: After Wadi Al-Qura and Taima', he returned to Madinah in late Safar or early Rabi' al-Awwal 7 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Platoons of 7 AH
commentary: Several small platoons: Ghalib bin 'Abdullah Al-Laithi against Bani Al-Muluh (Safar or Rabi' al-Awwal), 'Umar with thirty men to Turbah against Hawazin (Sha'ban), Basheer bin Sa'd with thirty men against Bani Murrah near Fadak (Sha'ban), Ghalib with 130 men against Bani 'Awal and Bani 'Abd bin Tha'labah (Ramadan), and Basheer with 300 men to Yemen and Jabar (Shawwal).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Expedition called Dhat-ur-Riqa‘ (in the year 7 A.H.)

title: Ghazwah of Dhat Ar-Riqa'
commentary: Hearing that Bani Muharib and Bani Tha'labah of Ghatfan were gathering, he marched into Najd with 400 or 700 men; no fighting took place, but he led the prayer of fear. The Companions bandaged their injured feet with rags, which gave the expedition its name.
notes: The book holds that it took place after the fall of Khaibar in 7 AH; some scholars place it in Rabi' Ath-Thani or Jumada Al-Ula 4 AH. The month here is estimated.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Expedition called Dhat-ur-Riqa‘ (in the year 7 A.H.)

title: The Compensatory 'Umrah ('Umrat Al-Qada')
commentary: As agreed at Al-Hudaibiyah, he went to Makkah with 2,000 men besides some women and children, and sixty camels for sacrifice. Quraish withdrew to the hills to watch, and on the fourth morning they asked him to leave, so he departed for Sarif.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Marriage to Maimunah bint Al-Harith
commentary: During this visit his uncle Al-'Abbas offered him the hand of Maimunah bint Al-Harith, sister of Umm Al-Fadl Lubabah. The Prophet accepted, and the wedding took place at Sarif.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Shuja' bin Wahb's expedition to Hawazin
commentary: Shuja' bin Wahb Al-Asadi led twenty-five men against Hawazin. It was a minor skirmish: they met no resistance and took some booty.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Battle of Mu'tah
commentary: After his envoy Al-Harith bin 'Umair Al-Azdi, carrying a letter to the ruler of Busra, was killed by Sharhabeel bin 'Amr Al-Ghassani, he sent 3,000 men under Zaid bin Harithah, then Ja'far, then 'Abdullah bin Rawaha.
They met a Byzantine and allied Arab army of 200,000. All three commanders were martyred; Khalid bin Al-Waleed, chosen as leader, withdrew the army skilfully, and only twelve Muslims were killed.
notes: The book gives Jumada Al-Ula 8 AH / September 629 CE.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Campaign of Dhat As-Salasil
commentary: 'Amr bin Al-'As led 300 Emigrants and Helpers against Quda'ah tribes on the Syrian border who were allied with the Byzantines. Reinforced by 200 men under Abu 'Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah, including Abu Bakr and 'Umar, he advanced deep into their land and scattered the enemy.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Expedition to Khadrah (Abu Qatadah)
commentary: Hearing that Ghatfan were massing troops, he sent Abu Qatadah with fifteen men. Within fifteen days they killed some, captured others and seized their property.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Quraish break the Hudaibiyah truce
commentary: Banu Bakr, allies of Quraish, attacked Khuza'ah, allies of the Muslims, at Al-Wateer by night, helped by Quraish with men and arms, and killed them even inside the Sanctuary. Abu Sufyan went to Madinah to renew the truce, but failed.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The army marches on Makkah
commentary: Keeping his aim secret, he left Madinah with 10,000 men. Al-'Abbas joined him at Al-Juhfa, and his cousin Abu Sufyan bin Al-Harith was pardoned on the way. At Marr Az-Zahran, Al-'Abbas brought Abu Sufyan bin Harb to him, and he accepted Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Preparations for the Attack on Makkah, and the Prophet’s Attempt at imposing a News Black-out

title: The Conquest of Makkah
commentary: The army entered Makkah from several sides, Khalid bin Al-Waleed from below, Az-Zubair from above and Abu 'Ubaidah with the infantry through a valley, with orders to fight only in self-defence. Anyone who stayed home, entered the Sacred Mosque or Abu Sufyan's house was safe.
He knocked down the 360 idols at the Ka'bah, had the images inside it removed, and Bilal gave the call to prayer from on top of it.
He pardoned the people of Makkah, saying "No reproach on you this day" (Yusuf 12:92), and stayed nineteen days.
notes: The book gives the morning of Tuesday 17 Ramadan 8 AH as the time he left Marr Az-Zahran for Makkah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Preparations for the Attack on Makkah, and the Prophet’s Attempt at imposing a News Black-out

title: Al-'Uzza, Suwa' and Manat destroyed
commentary: Soon after the conquest, Khalid bin Al-Waleed destroyed Al-'Uzza at Nakhlah, 'Amr bin Al-'As destroyed Suwa', the idol of Hudhail, and Sa'd bin Zaid Al-Ashhali destroyed Manat at Al-Mashallal.
notes: The book says all three were sent in Ramadan 8 AH; the day is estimated.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Preparations for the Attack on Makkah, and the Prophet’s Attempt at imposing a

title: Khalid among Banu Jadhimah
commentary: Khalid was sent with 350 horsemen to invite Banu Jadhimah to Islam peacefully. When they could not express their intention clearly, he killed some of them and took others captive. The Prophet said twice, "O Allah! I am innocent of what Khalid has done," and sent 'Ali, who paid blood-money for all their losses.
notes: The book says only 8 AH, after the conquest; the date here is estimated. The book's English text spells the tribe "Bani Khuzaimah".

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Preparations for the Attack on Makkah, and the Prophet’s Attempt at imposing a

title: The Battle of Hunain
commentary: Hawazin and Thaqif gathered under Malik bin 'Awf An-Nasri at Awtas. The Prophet marched with 12,000 men: the 10,000 of the conquest and 2,000 others, many of them Makkans who had recently embraced Islam.
Ambushed in the valley of Hunain before dawn, the army fled in confusion while he stood firm with a few. Al-'Abbas called the Companions back, they returned to the fight, and the enemy was routed.
notes: The army reached Hunain on the night of Wednesday 10 Shawwal.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Islamic Army stunned the Archers and the Attackers

title: Siege of At-Ta'if
commentary: The defeated Thaqif, with Malik bin 'Awf, fortified themselves in At-Ta'if. The siege lasted between 10 and 20 days, with a mangonel and the cutting and burning of their vineyards; twelve Muslims were killed. He then lifted the siege, praying: "O Allah, guide Thaqif and bring them to us as Muslims."
notes: Approximate dates. The book says the length of the siege is disputed but lies between 10 and 20 days.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Distribution of the booty at Al-Ji'ranah
commentary: Back at Al-Ji'ranah, he waited over ten nights for Hawazin to come before dividing the booty, then gave the largest shares to chiefs who had recently embraced Islam.

Some of the Helpers were upset until he asked them: "Are you not satisfied that the people go with ewes and camels while you go with the Messenger of Allah to your dwellings?" Hawazin's delegation then came as Muslims, and their women and children were returned to them.
notes: Approximate date.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: The Distribution of the Booty at Al-Ji‘ranah

title: 'Umrah from Al-Ji'ranah and return to Madinah
commentary: From Al-Ji'ranah he went to Makkah in the state of 'Umrah and performed it, appointed 'Itab bin Usaid governor of Makkah, and reached Madinah in the last six nights of Dhul-Qa'dah 8 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Lesser Pilgrimage (Al-‘Umrah) to Makkah and leaving for Madinah

title: Ka'b bin Zuhair accepts Islam
commentary: The poet Ka'b bin Zuhair, who had satirised the Prophet, was urged by his brother Bujair, after the return from At-Ta'if, to come in repentance. He came to Madinah, was pardoned as a Muslim, and recited his poem "Su'ad appeared..." in praise of the Prophet.
notes: The book dates this to 8 AH, after the return from At-Ta'if; the month is estimated.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Collectors sent to the tribes
commentary: As soon as the crescent of Muharram 9 AH appeared, he sent collectors to the tribes. The book lists sixteen, among them 'Uyaina bin Hisn to Bani Tamim, 'Adi bin Hatim to Tai' and Bani Asad, Al-'Ala' bin Al-Hadrami to Al-Bahrain, and 'Ali bin Abi Talib to Najran to collect Sadaqa and Jizya.
notes: The book also says some of these agents were dispatched in Muharram 7 AH and others later, until their tribes had fully embraced Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Platoons of 9 AH
commentary: 'Uyaina bin Hisn with fifty horsemen against Banu Tamim, who then accepted Islam (Muharram); Qutbah bin 'Amir to Khath'am (Safar); Ad-Dahhak bin Sufyan to Banu Kilab (Rabi' al-Awwal); and 'Alqamah bin Mujazziz with three hundred men to the Jeddah coast against Abyssinian pirates (Rabi' al-Akhir).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of Umm Kulthum, his daughter
commentary: His daughter Umm Kulthum, wife of 'Uthman, died. The Prophet felt extremely sad and told 'Uthman that had he a third daughter, he would marry her to him.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Some Important Events that featured that Year

title: The Year of Delegations
commentary: The delegations recorded by the biographers numbered over seventy. A few came before the conquest of Makkah, but most came after it, mainly in 9 and 10 AH and in greatest numbers after Tabuk. Among them were Hamdan, Fazarah, Tujeeb and Tai', and a message came from the kings of Himyar.
notes: The book adds that some delegations did not arrive until 11 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Christian delegation of Najran
commentary: A delegation of sixty men from Najran refused Islam and asked about Jesus. After Aal 'Imran 3:59-61 was revealed, he proposed a mutual invocation of curses (mubahalah). They declined it and made peace on paying tribute of two thousand garments, and he sent Abu 'Ubaidah bin Al-Jarrah to collect it.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Delegation of Banu Hanifah with Musailimah
commentary: Seventeen men of Banu Hanifah came, including Musailimah, who wanted the Prophet to make him his successor. He later claimed prophethood in 10 AH and was killed in the battle of Al-Yamamah in Rabi' al-Awwal 12 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Delegations of 'Udhrah and Bali
commentary: Twelve men of 'Udhrah came in Safar and the Bali delegation in Rabi' al-Awwal. Both accepted Islam and stayed three days.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: 'Ali destroys Al-Qullus; 'Adi bin Hatim accepts Islam
commentary: 'Ali led 150 men to destroy Al-Qullus, the idol of Tai'. 'Adi bin Hatim fled to Ash-Sham, but his sister, who was among the captives and was treated generously by the Prophet, urged him to go to Madinah, where he accepted Islam.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Expedition of Tabuk
commentary: On news that the Byzantines and their Ghassanid allies were mustering a huge army, he openly called the Muslims to march, in a time of drought and great heat. 'Uthman, Abu Bakr and others gave generously, and on a Thursday an army of 30,000 marched north.

The Byzantines did not dare come out. He stayed twenty days at Tabuk, and the people of Ailah, Jarba' and Adhruh made peace and paid tribute. The expedition lasted fifty days and was his last invasion.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of the Negus Ashamah
commentary: The Negus Ashamah, king of Abyssinia, died. The Prophet announced his death and performed the funeral prayer for him in absentia.
notes: The book dates it to Rajab 9 AH, shortly after Tabuk, and also lists it among the events of 9 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The three who stayed behind
commentary: Ka'b bin Malik, Murarah bin Ar-Rabi' and Hilal bin Umaiyah told the truth that they had no excuse. The Prophet forbade the people to speak to them; after more than forty days they were told to keep away from their wives, and after fifty days Allah accepted their repentance (At-Tawbah 9:118).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Thaqif accept Islam
commentary: Their chief 'Urwah bin Mas'ud had accepted Islam and was killed by his own people when he called them to it. After Tabuk, Thaqif sent a delegation of six men to Madinah and accepted Islam. A party under Khalid bin Al-Waleed, with Al-Mughirah bin Shu'bah, demolished the idol Al-Lat.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of 'Abdullah bin Ubai
commentary: 'Abdullah bin Abi Salool (Ubai), head of the hypocrites, died after the return from Tabuk. The Prophet asked Allah's forgiveness for him and prayed over him despite 'Umar's objection; a Qur'anic verse later confirmed 'Umar's view.
notes: The book says only that it was after the return from Tabuk (Ramadan 9 AH); the month is an estimate.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam
source.section: Some Important Events that featured that Year

title: Abu Bakr leads the Hajj; Bara'ah proclaimed
commentary: Abu Bakr was sent to lead the pilgrimage. The opening passages of Surah At-Tawbah (Bara'ah) were then revealed, and 'Ali, sent after him, proclaimed at Al-Jamrah on the day of sacrifice the end of covenants with the idolaters, giving them four months' respite. Abu Bakr had it announced that no disbeliever would perform Hajj after that year and no one would circle the Ka'bah naked.
notes: The book says Abu Bakr was sent in Dhul-Qa'dah or Dhul-Hijjah 9 AH.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Mu'adh bin Jabal sent to Yemen
commentary: Sending Mu'adh to Yemen in 10 AH, he told him he might not see him after that year, and might pass by his mosque and his tomb. Mu'adh wept for fear of parting from him.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of his son Ibrahim
commentary: Ibrahim, his son by his concubine Mariyah the Copt, died in Madinah while still a little child.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Farewell Pilgrimage (Hajjat Al-Wada')
commentary: He announced his pilgrimage, and huge crowds came to Madinah to join him. He set out on a Saturday in the last days of Dhul-Qa'dah, spent the night at Dhul-Hulaifah and entered ihram there, and reached Makkah on Sunday 4 Dhul-Hijjah, after eight days on the way.

He performed Hajj and 'Umrah together (Qiran). He went to Mina on the 8th and 'Arafah on the 9th, spent the Tashreeq days in Mina and left it on the 13th, then made the Farewell Tawaf and returned to Madinah.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Sermon at 'Arafah
commentary: At 'Arafah, before a crowd the book puts at 124,000 or 144,000, he declared lives and property sacred, abolished the blood-revenge and usury of the pre-Islamic era, urged them to fear Allah concerning women, and said he had left among them the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.
After the sermon the verse "This day I have perfected your religion for you" (Al-Ma'idah 5:3) was revealed.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The Sermon on the Day of Sacrifice
commentary: On the morning of the Day of Sacrifice, mounted on a grey mule, he delivered another sermon, which 'Ali relayed to the people. He explained the four sacred months, declared blood, property and honour as inviolable as that day, month and town, and told those present to convey it to those absent.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: The last delegation: An-Nakha'
commentary: Two hundred men of An-Nakha' arrived in the middle of Muharram 11 AH; they were the last delegation to reach him.
notes: The book says "the middle of Muharram"; the day is an estimate.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Usamah bin Zaid's army is raised
commentary: In Safar 11 AH he mobilised a great army under Usamah bin Zaid to the borders of Al-Balqa' and Ad-Darum in Palestine. When people criticised Usamah's youth, he defended his leadership. News of the Prophet's illness held the army back, and it became the first expedition sent out under Abu Bakr's caliphate.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Farewell prayer for the martyrs of Uhud
commentary: In the early days of Safar he went out to Uhud and offered a farewell prayer for the martyrs, as if bidding farewell to the living and the dead. He then told the people from the pulpit that he would precede them and they would meet him at the Fountain, and that he did not fear they would turn to polytheism, but that worldly riches would lead them to fight one another.
notes: The book says "the early days of Safar"; the day is an estimate.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: His final illness begins
commentary: On Monday 29 Safar 11 AH he attended a funeral at Al-Baqi'; on the way back he had a headache and a high fever.
He led the prayers for eleven days while ill. His illness lasted thirteen or fourteen days, and he spent the last week in 'Aishah's room.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Abu Bakr leads the prayers
commentary: From the evening of Thursday, four days before his death, he was too ill to go out to the mosque and ordered Abu Bakr to lead the prayers; Abu Bakr led seventeen prayers in his lifetime. When 'Aishah repeatedly asked him to excuse Abu Bakr, he refused.
notes: Thursday 8 to Monday 12 Rabi' al-Awwal, counted back from his death on Monday 12 Rabi' al-Awwal.

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Death of the Prophet ﷺ
commentary: He died at high morning in 'Aishah's house, leaning against her, saying "the most exalted Companionship on high". He was sixty-three years and four days old.
'Umar refused to believe it until Abu Bakr recited "Muhammad is no more than a Messenger" (Aal 'Imran 3:144).

source.book: Ar-Raheeq Al-Makhtum (The Sealed Nectar), Safiur-Rahman Al-Mubarakpuri, English tr. Issam Diab, Darussalam

title: Abu Bakr chosen as Caliph; burial
commentary: At the portico of Banu Sa'idah the Emigrants and Helpers, after long discussion, acknowledged Abu Bakr as Caliph.

On Tuesday his body was washed with his clothes on and shrouded in three white cotton cloths. People entered ten at a time to pray over him, and he was buried where he died, in 'Aishah's room, in the night before Wednesday.
hijri-date: 12-14 Rabi' al-Awwal 11 AH (Monday to Wednesday night)
